mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, triggering a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations fall, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% month-over-month, or the joint Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic contractions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity, leading to reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.0 during late-cycle contractions, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving consumer confidence and residential investment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 275.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 275.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, reducing household income and consumption, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the joint Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-2001 recession recovery phase, a declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 5.0% indicates continued monetary accommodation, supporting economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during the post-2001 recession recovery when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.
